turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Come on in, both of you. Howzit. What's brought you down today?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Shame, doctor, it's my stomach. My niece's wedding was on Saturday in the Midlands, a gorgeous do, and since then I've had diarrhoea and I've been vomiting.
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): Okay. Tell me the story from the beginning, no rush.

[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): We drove up on the Friday. There was a robot out near the highway and we sat in Thandi's bakkie for ages, and my knee was not impressed. The venue had fairy lights in the trees, and the DJ was stuck in the eighties, which I actually didn't mind.
[SEG0005] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Ma, he doesn't need the DJ.
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja, ja. The meal was a buffet, prawns, a chicken dish, pasta in a cream sauce. I had a bit of everything, you do at a wedding.
[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): Sunday morning I was up and I thought I was fine, and then the diarrhoea hit. I vomited twice before lunch that day.
[SEG0008] person_3 (CAREGIVER): It wasn't Sunday. You were already running to the bathroom Saturday night after the prawns. This is day four, not two.
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): That's not right. I was dancing on Saturday night. It started Sunday morning, and this is the third morning, so two full days, not four.
[SEG0010] person_1 (DOCTOR): Alright, we'll park the exact start for a moment. The diarrhoea itself, roughly how many times are we talking?

[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): Um, I lost count, hey. Yesterday maybe six or seven, could be eight if you count one that was mostly wind. This morning I'd already been three times before we left, and I stopped counting after the rooibos.
[SEG0012] person_1 (DOCTOR): And the vomiting, how has that been for you?
[SEG0013] person_3 (CAREGIVER): She can't keep anything down. She's been vomiting the whole time, even water comes straight back up. Nothing has stayed in since yesterday.

[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): Ag, Thandi, no. I vomited three times in total, twice on Sunday and once last night. This morning I kept the rooibos and a bit of toast, so I'm not vomiting the whole time.
[SEG0015] person_1 (DOCTOR): It's good the tea stayed down. Was there any blood in the vomit, or dark coffee-ground material?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): No, nothing like that. It was food the first time, then just bitter fluid.
[SEG0017] person_1 (DOCTOR): And in the stool, have you seen any blood, or black tarry stool?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): Mm, I suppose... sometimes, not really. The pasta sauce was red, and I wasn't exactly studying it.
[SEG0019] person_1 (DOCTOR): We'll leave that as unclear, then. Any fever, or times you felt properly hot?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): No fever. I checked with the thermometer at home and it was normal, thirty six point something. I was a bit shivery, but I didn't have a temperature.
[SEG0021] person_1 (DOCTOR): Is there pain in the tummy along with it?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): Crampy, low down, mostly just before I have to go. It eases off a bit once I've been. Not agony, just nasty cramps.
[SEG0023] person_1 (DOCTOR): What about fluids, have you managed to drink?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): If I sip, yes. A big gulp came back last night. Well, actually that was the last big vomit, and sipping was fine this morning, though I'm proper thirsty.
[SEG0025] person_3 (CAREGIVER): I didn't see her drink much at the house. I wasn't in the kitchen the whole morning, to be fair.
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): I drank in the kitchen, Thandi. And I haven't peed since last night, which is not like me.
[SEG0027] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any burning when you do pass water, or is it only that there's less?
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): No burning. Just less of it, and quite dark. Sorry, that's a bit gross to say out loud.
[SEG0029] person_1 (DOCTOR): Not gross at all, it's helpful. Any long-term problems, or medicines you take regularly?

[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): Blood pressure, I've had that for years. I take amlodipine, five milligrams, every morning. And last year, when I went in for my knee, they did bloods and the doctor said my cholesterol was borderline, so I was meant to ease off the rich food, and then a wedding comes along.
[SEG0031] person_1 (DOCTOR): What was done for the knee?

[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): Oh, just arthritis. They injected it, they didn't operate. The physio was a lovely woman from Durban, and we spent the session on her son's rugby, he plays flyhalf, she's very proud.
[SEG0033] person_3 (CAREGIVER): She's also been taking Imodium, doctor. The pharmacist at Clicks told her not to, because if it's a tummy bug from food you mustn't block it up. She took it anyway.
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): I just wanted to sleep, that's all. It's loperamide, the capsules, two milligrams on the box. Yesterday I took one after each time I went.

[SEG0035] person_3 (CAREGIVER): It was two capsules each time. I popped them out for you, so that's four milligrams a go. The clinic sister said the same last winter, don't use stoppers for food poisoning.

[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): The very first dose was two capsules, because that's what the packet says to start with, and after that it was one. So it was two milligrams, not four, except right at the beginning.
[SEG0037] person_3 (CAREGIVER): I put two capsules in your hand every time I was with you. I'm not going to stand here and say I didn't see it.

[SEG0038] person_1 (DOCTOR): Whatever the exact number, you've been using loperamide after you were told not to. Please stop it now. If this is infectious diarrhoea we usually let it come out, rather than corking it up early on.
[SEG0039] person_2 (PATIENT): If you say so. It wasn't even helping, hey. I still had to run.
[SEG0040] person_1 (DOCTOR): Has anyone else from the wedding come down with the same thing?

[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja, my sister, and two cousins on the groom's side. My sister phoned this morning with the same running and vomiting. We didn't cook, so it isn't my food, and the auntie who made the pasta is mortified, shame.

[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): The cake was lemon, three tiers, and the little one nearly went when the dog shot past. I'm retired, I taught for thirty years, so I notice when a cake is about to fall. You don't need the dog story, sorry.
[SEG0043] person_1 (DOCTOR): The dog can wait until you're better. Did you eat anything odd on the drive up, or have you been overseas lately?

[SEG0044] person_2 (PATIENT): No overseas. We just did two nights at a guesthouse in the Midlands. I thought the Sunday eggs looked dodgy, but I felt ill before breakfast. Well, actually, I only felt properly ill after breakfast, so I'm mixing myself up.
[SEG0045] person_3 (CAREGIVER): The eggs were fine, I ate them too. She told me the prawns tasted funny.
[SEG0046] person_2 (PATIENT): I said they were rich, not funny. I still ate them. They were lekker, if I'm honest, a bit too lekker.
[SEG0047] person_1 (DOCTOR): Let me have a look at you. I'll start with the numbers.

[SEG0048] person_1 (DOCTOR): Blood pressure is one eighteen over seventy four. Pulse is one hundred and four, a little quick. Temperature is thirty seven point one, and oxygen saturation is ninety eight percent.

[SEG0049] person_1 (DOCTOR): Your tongue and lips are dry. The tummy is soft, mildly tender across the lower part, with no guarding, and the bowel sounds are active. I'd call this mild dehydration, not a severe picture.

[SEG0050] person_2 (PATIENT): I knew my mouth was dry, it tastes like the bottom of a birdcage. Is a pulse of one hundred and four dangerous? My brother had a heart thing and his pulse was all over, but that was after his bypass, and he lives in PE now, so it's a different story.
[SEG0051] person_1 (DOCTOR): One hundred and four is not dangerous in this setting. It fits with being a bit dry and unwell. Do you feel dizzy when you stand up?
[SEG0052] person_2 (PATIENT): Mm, I suppose. Sometimes, not really. If I stand up fast after the toilet, but I'm tired more than dizzy.
[SEG0053] person_1 (DOCTOR): Then we won't record that as dizziness. You last passed urine last night, is that right?
[SEG0054] person_2 (PATIENT): About ten last night. Nothing since, and it was dark yellow that time.

[SEG0055] person_1 (DOCTOR): I think this is most likely a food-related gastroenteritis from that wedding meal, given your sister and the cousins are ill too, with mild dehydration on top. The two of you don't quite agree whether it's been two days or four, but either way it's acute. I can't name the exact bug from here.
[SEG0056] person_2 (PATIENT): So it's not the cholesterol, then. They said borderline, and I always worry that means worse. The letter never gave me a number I remember, just that word, borderline.
[SEG0057] person_1 (DOCTOR): A borderline cholesterol from last year does not cause this. It's a different problem. Have you kept the amlodipine down, the five milligrams in the morning?
[SEG0058] person_2 (PATIENT): This morning, yes, it stayed down with the toast. Yesterday I took it and I think I brought it up, but I'm not a hundred percent sure. The day before was fine.
[SEG0059] person_3 (CAREGIVER): She didn't take yesterday's. I found the tablet still sitting in the little cup on the counter this morning. So it was missed, not vomited.
[SEG0060] person_2 (PATIENT): Was it really? I could have sworn I swallowed it. My head is porridge this week, sorry doctor.

[SEG0061] person_1 (DOCTOR): It's easy to lose track when you're this ill. If this morning's dose stayed down, carry on each morning as long as you can keep it in. If you vomit a tablet, don't double the next one, just wait until the following day.
[SEG0062] person_2 (PATIENT): Lekker. Thandi can watch me swallow it so we don't have another fight about it.

[SEG0063] person_1 (DOCTOR): Fluids are the real treatment here. Please get an oral rehydration solution, Rehidrat or Hydrol, from the chemist, and take small sips, a mouthful every few minutes, aiming for around a litre and a half over the day if you can. Water and rooibos in between are fine, but skip fizzy cooldrinks and fruit juice for now, because they can worsen the diarrhoea.
[SEG0064] person_2 (PATIENT): Around a litre and a half, okay. Hydrol is the orange one, I think. My neighbour swears by flat Coke, though.
[SEG0065] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'd rather you didn't use flat Coke, it's an old idea. When you feel like food, keep it plain, toast, rice, banana. No braai chops for a few days, I'm afraid.

[SEG0066] person_2 (PATIENT): The wedding was the best food I've had all year and now I can't look at a chop. There was a potato salad with mustard that I'm still dreaming about, the auntie puts a secret in it.

[SEG0067] person_1 (DOCTOR): Save the potato salad for when you're well. I don't need blood tests today, you're not dry enough for that. If the diarrhoea hasn't settled in the next two or three days, or if you start keeping nothing at all down, we might send a stool sample to look for a bug.
[SEG0068] person_2 (PATIENT): Not today? I brought a sample in a jar, it's in the bakkie, Thandi made me. It's probably cooked, the car was sitting in the sun.
[SEG0069] person_3 (CAREGIVER): It's in a cooler bag, don't be dramatic. It is from this morning, though.

[SEG0070] person_1 (DOCTOR): I won't send that jar. If we do a stool test it should be a fresh sample in a proper lab container, not one that's been riding in the car. So that's only if things are not settling, not today.
[SEG0071] person_2 (PATIENT): And if I see blood for real, not me imagining the tomato sauce?

[SEG0072] person_1 (DOCTOR): If you see clear blood, or you can't manage to sip fluids, or you're too dizzy to stand, or there's no urine for a whole day, come straight in and don't wait. Otherwise, if you're not better in three days, come back and see me and we'll arrange that stool test.
[SEG0073] person_2 (PATIENT): Three days I can do, if the sipping works. Thank you, doctor. Come on, Thandi, before I start on the dog again.

spec.situation: Diarrhoea and vomiting after a trip or a wedding meal; others at the event are ill; patient counts bowel movements loosely; takes loperamide against advice; mild dehydration signs; stool test conditional; advice on fluids.
features: ambiguous_answer: an answer that sounds like yes but is really 'maybe' ('mm, I suppose', 'sometimes, not really'); recorded with uncertainty or not at all, never as a firm fact.
hedged_plan: the doctor hedges ('we might do a scan if it does not settle', 'let's see in two weeks'). Conditional vs planned status must follow the words.
relative_speaks_for_patient: a relative answers for the patient and the patient partly contradicts; reported_by follows who said it.
test_result_recalled: the patient reports an old test or result ('they said it was borderline'); recorded as reported history/investigation only as far as said, not as a confirmed value.

bad.reason: Knee injection is supported, but timeframe 'last year' is not clearly stated for the injection.

omissions.text: Vomiting details are incorrectly captured as current/ongoing uncertainty only; the patient specifically reported vomiting 3 times total: twice on Sunday and once last night, with no vomiting this morning and rooibos plus a bit of toast kept down.
Loperamide dose/use details missing: patient said the box was 2 mg capsules; first dose was 2 capsules initially, then 1 capsule after each subsequent diarrhoeal episode, and it was not helping.
Negative finding asked and answered but not recorded: no coffee-ground material/dark vomit; vomit was food initially then bitter fluid.
Negative finding asked and answered but not recorded: black tarry stool denied/unclear together with blood in stool being unclear.
Shivery/chills without measured fever were reported.
Fluid tolerance detail missing: able to drink if sipping; large gulps provoked vomiting last night, but sipping was fine this morning.
Examination/assessment finding not separately recorded: doctor assessed mild dehydration and specifically said it was not a severe picture.
Negative finding from examination not recorded: no severe abdominal picture, specifically no guarding with soft abdomen and only mild lower tenderness.
History supporting likely infectious foodborne illness not fully recorded: sister and two cousins from the wedding also developed similar diarrhoea/vomiting.
Plan detail missing: doctor said no blood tests were needed today because the patient was not dehydrated enough.

Investigation plan/detail missing: patient had brought a stool sample jar, but doctor explicitly declined to send it and said any stool test later would need a fresh sample in a proper lab container, not one kept in the car.
